en: AI agents typically expose tools to large
language models so that the large language
models can request the use of certain tools.
Now, one very powerful tool which
applications like ChatGPT, for example, if
you install it on your system,
expose to large language models is the
computer use tool.
And the idea here is that,
of course, for a model to help you,
it must be able to
use your computer as you could use it,
because that would also allow the model to
perform tasks that are maybe primarily built
for humans. Because the idea behind the
computer use tool is that software like
ChatGPT is able to record your screen or
take screenshots of your screen, show that
to the model, and then ask the model what it
wants to do next in order to perform a
certain task. And based on that screen
recording, the model can then decide to move
the mouse to to a certain position, then
make a click,
and so on.
Therefore, computer use is also a quite
inefficient tool because it constantly needs
to make a screenshot, analyze the
screenshot, move the mouse, click, analyze
the result, and so on. That's not very
efficient.
And for example, for reading a file, it's
much faster if the application exposes a
read file tool which uses code to find and
open and analyze the file. But for certain
tasks, or certain pieces of software that
may be installed on your system, there may
just not be a better way of using it than
replicating computer use as you as a human
would use it. And that's why some agentic
software like the ChatGPT software, but also
the Claude software, for example, ships with
such a computer use tool, which gives an AI
model this way of using a computer as you
would use it. Again, not very efficient, but
very powerful.
